title: Sparkline output playbook — personal OKR scratchpad
body:
Purpose
---
This is a lightweight 6-week personal OKR + weekly-checkin scratchpad. Goal: maintain steady output (ship items), protect energy for deep work, and create 3 repeatable rituals that lower context switching. Not a polished PRD — very much a living notebook.

Metrics I care about (compact)
- Output index: completed tickets / planned tickets per week (target >= 0.75)
- Impact score (subjective, 1-5 per week; target avg >= 3.5)
- Energy score (daily quick rating 1-5; weekly avg target >= 3.6)
- Noisy-alerts reduced: p99 alert noise count (target: -30% vs baseline)
- Learning: number of inference/serving papers read (target 6 in 6 weeks)

6-week plan (hypothesis-driven)
Week 0 (setup): clarify 3 ship goals, calendar blocks, lightweight test harness for local perf experiments.
Week 1–2: ship Goal A (canary rollout for KV cache telemetry), run microbenchmarks, capture baseline latency distribution.
Week 3–4: ship Goal B (prefix caching experiment + docs for team), measure cost delta.
Week 5–6: ship Goal C (reduce alert noise by tuning SRE thresholds + small automation), run retrospective and finalize learning notes.

Weekly check-in template (short)
- Week: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD
- Wins (bullet):
- Roadblocks (bullet, what I need from others):
- Energy avg / Output index / Impact score:
- Quick plan for next week (3 things):

Example: Week 1 check-in (2026-01-19 to 2026-01-25)
- Wins: Implemented basic KV cache metrics into telemetry agent; 2 small unit tests; demo to Noah.
- Roadblocks: Need SRE to grant temporary access to prod metrics (filed INF-842).
- Metrics: Energy 3.8 / Output 0.8 / Impact 4
- Plan: Finish dashboards for cache hit rate, write short blurb for Console docs, run two microbench runs on g4dn.

Retro notes (ongoing)
- What worked: Short daily 60-minute deep blocks on mornings preserved focus. Quick async triage channel (ping-ops) reduced meetings.
- What failed: Tried to batch too many small PRs into one deployment window — increased risk and slowed review velocity.
- Adjust: Ship more small, independent PRs; use feature flags aggressively.

Experiments (tracked)
- Microbatching window swing: compare continuous-batching window of 8ms vs 25ms for short prompts; measure p50/p95 and cost per token. (Experiment id: exp-spark-01)
- Prefix caching eviction heuristics: LRU vs time-decay weighting; track hit rate and mismatch regressions. (exp-spark-02)
- Calendar trial: morning deep block (8–10am) vs afternoon deep block (2–4pm) for two weeks; track energy and output.

Action items (immediate)
- [ ] Finalize KV cache dashboard (owner: me) — due 2026-01-22
- [ ] Follow up on INF-842 (owner: Noah) — pending SRE approval
- [ ] Draft Console how-to note for the team (owner: me) — due 2026-01-29
- [ ] Read/annotate two inference papers this week (owner: me)

Notes to self (choppy)
- Keep check-ins short, try 3 bullets per section.
- If energy dips below 3 for two days, allow a recovery day (walk, email-free afternoon).
- Don’t optimize microcosts before validating traffic pattern changes.

Questions / open decisions
- How aggressive to be with cache TTL reductions for dedicated customers? Risk: correctness vs gain in cost. Need PM input from Maya.
- Is there bandwidth to run small dedicated infra runs on weekends for stable baselines? (Ops cost + credit).

References and quick links
- Confluence notes for rollout: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/INFER-ops-checklist
- Jira ticket for SRE access: JIRA:INF-842
- PR with telemetry changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prod-deployments/pull/237

Last thoughts (end-of-day ritual)
- Write 3 short sentences about impact today. If none, write one note about a blocker and next step. This helps keep the momentum and avoids over-indexing on long weekly docs.

(End of scratchpad — will refine after Week 6 retro)
